summary: Iteration 17 — Full test of the unified Audit Log rewrite (backend + frontend). Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_audit_logs.py with 16 pytest cases covering shape, platform filter, client filter, action-bucket collapse (invite + onboarding), entity_type/user_id/date/q filters, pagination, admin-only 403s (contributor + readonly), platform_admin scoping (unauthorized-client 403 + default scope), facets shape (11 buckets + non-empty clients), and CSV export headers/content-disposition. All 16 pass (16/16). Frontend: end-to-end Playwright as super_admin — sidebar label is 'Audit Log' (data-testid=nav-admin-audit), legacy nav-audit absent; /admin/audit renders all filters + audit-search + audit-export + audit-table with 50 rows; count line '1,355 events · Page 1 of 28'; row click opens audit-detail drawer with all documented fields (event/raw/at/client/user/entity/entity-id); Platform Activity filter reduces to 11 rows all with Platform badge; Invited filter first row shows 'Contact Invited'; Next paginates to page 2; Export CSV downloads audit-log.csv; ClientSettings → 'View Audit History' navigates to /admin/audit?client=<id>. Contributor: no nav-audit and no nav-admin-audit; /audit redirects to /dashboard; /admin/audit redirects to /dashboard (InternalOnly). All acceptance criteria met.

issues: Radix DialogContent warns 'Missing Description or aria-describedby' — non-blocking a11y warning; add SheetDescription (or aria-describedby) for the sheet.

action_items: Optional a11y polish: add a <SheetDescription> (or aria-describedby) inside AdminAudit.jsx AuditDetailDrawer to silence the Radix warning.
critical_code_review_comments: export_audit_csv reuses list_audit filter machinery but paginates 200-at-a-time up to 50 pages — fine for the 10k cap but the inner call re-runs the users/clients enrichment lookups per page; consider a single aggregation or shared cache to reduce round trips when tenants grow.

audit-log detail drawer only renders prev/next blocks when meta has those exact keys; the check falls back to previous/before + new/after — good, but the ClientSettings deep link relies on ?client=<id> being read by useSearchParams which currently works only because the parameter name matches ('client'). Keep those constants in one place if the query key ever changes.
list_audit uses regex from `q` with re.escape — safe. Good.
